sentences.text:
Heard counsel for the applicants, Sri Satyanand Tripathi, counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and
Sri Neeraj Kumar Sharma, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2.  The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet dated 17.11.2021 as well as the summoning/cognizance order dated 11.05.2022 and the entire proceedings of Case Crime No. 366 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Medical College, District- Meerut.

sentences.text: Considering that the matter had emanated from a matrimonial dispute between the husband and the wife, vide order dated 07.11.2023 passed by this Court, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre of this Court for exploring the possibility of settlement between the parties.
4. As per the report of the Mediation Centre dated 20.01.2024, the parties voluntarily arrived at a compromise.
The relevant paragraphs of the settlement agreement are extracted below;
"6. The parties hereto confirm and declare that they have voluntarily and of their own free will arrived at this Settlement Agreement in the presence of the Mediators/Conciliators.

7. In view of the Interim Settlement Agreement dated 06.01.2024, the following settlement has been arrived at between the Parties hereto:-
a) That the parties have settled their dispute and decided to live separately and in this regard they have filed a petition u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Ghaziabad and the same is registered as Case No. 98 of 2024.
The parties stated that all the terms and conditions mentioned therein have been fulfilled.
They further reiterated and reaffirm the terms and conditions of the aforesaid settlement and the same shall be a part of the settlement also.
The certified copy of the aforesaid divorce petition is being annexed to this settlement-agreement for kind perusal of the Hon'ble Court.

b) That it has been agreed between the parties that the applicant no. 1-husband shall pay one time settlement amount of Rs. 15,00,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakh Only)
which includes permanent alimony and Stridhan of the wife by way of Demand Draft.

c) That on 06.01.2024, the applicant no. 1-husband has produced a demand draft bearing no. 646321 dated 03.01.2024 for Rs. 4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakh Only)
drawn on State Bank of India in favour of Shipra Singh (wife), which was kept in the file concerned with the consent of the parties and today i.e. 20.01.2024 the same has been handed over to the Shipra Singh (wife) and she has acknowledged the receipt of the same.
d) That on 20.01.2024, the applicant no. 1-husband has handed over another demand draft bearing no. 646323 dated 15.01.2024 for Rs. 4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakh Only) drawn on State Bank of India in favour of Shipra Singh (wife) and she has acknowledged the receipt of the same.

e) That it has been agreed between the parties that the remaining amount i.e. Rs.
7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakh only) shall be paid by Shri Abhinav Singh Verma (Applicant No. 1- Husband) to Smt. Shipra Singh (O.P. No. 2-Wife) at the time of final judgment in Case No. 98 of 2024 pending in Family Court, Ghaziabad by way of demand draft.

2 f)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That it has also been agreed between the parties that all civil and criminal cases filed by them against each other regarding present matrimonial dispute shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the Court/authority concerned.
g) That the parties will not file any fresh case against each other in respect of this matrimonial dispute.
They have no claim against each other in future also.
h) That it has been agreed between the parties that they shall not violate the terms and conditions of this settlement otherwise the aggrieved party will be free to take legal recourse.

8. By signing this Agreement the Parties hereto state that the Application U/S 482 No. 38910 of 2023 and all disputes and differences in this regard have been amicably settled by the Parties hereto through the process of Conciliation/ Mediation."
5.
Counsel for the opposite party no. 2 submits that opposite party no. 2 has no objection if the proceedings are quashed.

6. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing a prosecution to proceed any further.
7.

Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T. 2008(9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.
